subject: FerrumPay discovery — cost levers, budget constraints, immediate next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kovac <elena@ferrumpay.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco@ferrumpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap and cost-focused next steps from today

Elena / Marco — thanks again for the time today. Short post-call recap focused on the economics and the concrete next steps we discussed. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain and goals
- Pain: inference spend variability hitting the payments P&L — peak hours driving >65% of monthly token costs and unpredictability in batch sizes across endpoints.
- Goal: demonstrate a pilot that reduces per-API-token cost by >=40% while keeping 95th percentile latency under 200ms for auth/lookups.

Observed signals you shared
- Monthly token volume: ~1.6B tokens (Q2 avg), with 30% of calls being short (<=16 tokens) and 10% very long (>1k tokens).
- Current infra: single cloud region, mix of CPU and small GPU endpoints; no prefix caching.
- Budget constraint: procurement has a $150k quarter budget for PoC infrastructure & credits.

Immediate cost levers we recommend for the pilot
1) Batching policy: 50–200ms micro-batch window for short calls (expected token-cost reduction 20–30%).
2) Prefix/KV caching for lookup-heavy flows (expected reduction on repeated prefixes 25–45%).
3) Model tiering + quantization: route prediction/lookups to a quantized 4-bit variant and reserve larger models for long-form generation — projected 10–20% savings on gen calls.
4) Autoscaling + reserved slots for peak windows to avoid expensive on-demand fallbacks.

Pilot success metrics (proposal)
- Cost: >=40% reduction in $/1000 tokens for the target flows within 30 days of pilot start.
- Latency: 95th <=200ms for lookups, P99 degradation <2x.
- Reliability: <1% error rate for production-like traffic during pilot windows.

Next steps (mutual action items)
- FerrumPay: share last 30 days of anonymized per-endpoint token histogram + any SLOs by July 6. (Action: Elena)
- Redwood: deliver a tailored TCO scenario (batching + cache + quantization) and a pilot story + ops checklist by July 5. (Action: Jonas / Marissa)
- Procurement: confirm whether the $150k is available for pilot spend + any required PO language by July 9. (Action: Marco)

Attachments: a quick usage snapshot template is attached — please fill or confirm numbers where you can.

If the above looks right I'll send the TCO scenario and a one-page pilot plan tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Elena — looping in a condensed TCO scenario and the operational checklist we'll use during the pilot. High-level callouts below; full PDF attached.

TCO scenario (high level)
- Baseline: no batching, no cache, gen-tier model only -> normalized cost = 1.0
- Scenario A (micro-batching + cache): estimated normalized cost = 0.58 (approx 42% savings)
- Scenario B (tiered models + quant): estimated normalized cost = 0.47 (approx 53% savings)

Assumptions (short)
- Token mix: 35% short (<16), 55% medium (16–512), 10% long (>512) per Elena's updated numbers.
- Batch window: 100ms default for lookups; aggressive 250ms for non-SLA critical batch jobs.
- Cache hit rate: modeled at 30% initially, with engineering improvements pushing to 50% over 30 days.

Pilot ops checklist (sample)
- Deliverables: ingested usage CSV, Redwood TCO PDF (attached), pilot config repo, rollback policy.
- Roles: FerrumPay eng owner (Marco), Redwood SE (Marissa), Account exec (Jonas).
- Success review: 30-day readout + go/no-go decision.

Attachments: redwood-tco-scenario.pdf (preview)

I'll convert this to a one-page decision brief and send to Elena + procurement contact after we get the confirmed numbers.

—Marissa
